# Candidate Show HN post

Title: Show HN: Drop in a folder of HTML and get back a private URL
Project URL: https://eze.page/
Posted (UTC): 2026-10-20T23:45:03Z

## Project page text (fetch status: ok)

```text
Turn a folder into a private website for your team.
eze is open-source hosting you run inside your company. Upload some HTML and get a link that only your coworkers can open. Every site gets a database, live updates, file uploads and AI, with nothing to set up.
Set it up
GitHub
Self-hosted. MIT license.
lunch-vote
index.html
poll.js
style.css
eze deploy
lunch-vote.eze.acme.com
Where should we eat on Friday?
Ramen place on 5th
9
Tacos
4
Salad bar
1
AN
BO
CY
DE
4 people from Acme are voting
How it works
Make a site
Write plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript yourself, or ask your AI tool to.
Deploy it
Run
eze deploy
or drop the folder on the eze dashboard.
Share the link
Anyone signed in to your company can open it. Nobody else can.
A backend without a backend
Pages load one script from eze and can save data, react to changes and know who is looking. They use the viewer's company sign-in, so there are no keys in your code.
<script src="/_q/sdk.js"></script>
<script type="module">
const me = await eze.id.me();
const votes = eze.db.collection('votes');
await votes.create({ place: 'Ramen', by: me.name });
votes.subscribe({ onCreate: (vote) => redraw() });
</script>
eze.db
Save and query data, with live updates
eze.files
Uploads like images, video and PDFs
eze.ws
Rooms for cursors, chat and games
eze.ai
Call Claude, OpenAI or your own model
eze.id
The name and email of whoever is viewing
Works with your AI tools
eze init
adds instructions that teach coding agents how to build an eze site.
eze mcp
lets Claude Code, Cursor and other MCP apps deploy sites for you.
claude mcp add eze -- eze mcp
> make a site where my team can vote
on where to eat on Friday
Set it up
You need a server, a domain with wildcard DNS and HTTPS, and your company's sign-in: Google Workspace, Okta, Entra ID or any OpenID Connect provider, or an auth proxy you already use.
eze is one program with a small database file. A small VM is plenty.
Read the setup guide
go install github.com/ahyield/eze/cmd/eze@latest
EZE_DOMAIN=eze.acme.com \
EZE_AUTH=oidc \
EZE_OIDC_ISSUER=https://accounts.google.com \
EZE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID=... \
EZE_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=... \
EZE_OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=acme.com \
EZE_SESSION_SECRET=... \
eze serve
Only for your company
Everyone who can sign in can open, change and redeploy every site. That keeps eze simple, so keep it to your own people: eze won't start if its sign-in would let in a public email domain like gmail.com.
Found a security problem?
Report it privately
.
```

## HN discussion (0 comments)

(no comments)

<think>Let me evaluate this candidate.

**Product**: `eze`, a self-hosted tool that lets you drop a folder of HTML/CSS/JS and get a private URL for your team.

**What it does**:
- Self-hosted (you run it inside your company), MIT license.
- Upload a folder (either via `eze deploy` or drop it on the dashboard).
- Every site gets: database, live updates, file uploads, AI, auth (who is viewing).
- SDK provides a simple API (`eze.id`, `eze.db`, `eze.files`, `eze.ws`, `eze.ai`).
- Works with auth providers like Google Workspace, Okta, Entra ID (OIDC).
- Also has MCP (`eze mcp`) so AI coding agents can deploy sites.

**Interesting features**:
- The "backend without a backend" idea — single SDK script lets pages save data, react to changes, know who is looking, use viewer's company sign-in. This is a very clever, fresh angle.
- It's designed specifically for internal company use ("Only for your company"), with a nice constraint: everyone can view/change/redeploy, which simplifies the permissions.
- It includes AI integrations and MCP support.
- Setup is a single binary with a small database file (SQLite under the hood, presumably).

**Why it's a push**:
1. Clever fresh angle on a familiar problem: building internal tools without a real backend. The idea that "you just write HTML/JS and the infrastructure gives you everything" is powerful and well-presented.
2. Useful sample of what people are building now: self-hosted internal tool platforms with auth + AI integrations.
3. Good creative way of explaining: the lunch-vote example and the clear "A backend without a backend" section.

I think this is worth a look — it's a well-scoped, nicely presented tool that solves a real need (internal tools) in a clever way.

Decision: push.

Reason: This is a clever "backend without a backend" idea — you just drop a folder of HTML/CSS/JS and get a private internal site with a database, auth, and AI, all via a single SDK script, which is a great, well-explained angle on a common problem.</think>{"decision": "push", "reason": "这是一个绝妙的“没有后端的后端”设想——你只需丢进去一个包含 HTML/CSS/JS 的文件夹，就能得到一个带有数据库、授权和 AI 功能的内部网站，全程只用一个 SDK 脚本，把常见问题处理得非常漂亮、直观。" }
